name: Tiberius
title: Emperor of the Roman Empire during Jesus' ministry
summary: Tiberius Julius Caesar Augustus was the second emperor of the Roman Empire and reigned from 14 to 37 AD. He is mentioned in the Bible as the emperor under whom John the Baptist began his ministry and Jesus Christ carried out his public work. His reign forms the political framework for the gospel narratives.

keyEvents.title: Tiberius' reign dates Jesus' ministry
keyEvents.description: The evangelist Luke dates the start of John the Baptist's ministry to the fifteenth year of Emperor Tiberius, providing an important chronological reference for Jesus' public work.

keyEvents.title: Tax to the emperor
keyEvents.description: Jesus was asked whether it was lawful to pay tax to the emperor (Tiberius). Jesus answered with the famous words about giving to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and to God what belongs to God.

keyEvents.title: Pontius Pilate as Tiberius' representative
keyEvents.description: Pontius Pilate served as Tiberius' prefect in Judea and sentenced Jesus to crucifixion. Jewish leaders pressured Pilate by implying that he was not the emperor's friend if he released Jesus.

keyEvents.title: The Emperor's Coin
keyEvents.description: The denarius shown to Jesus during the question about taxes bore Tiberius' image and inscription, illustrating the presence of Roman imperial power in daily life in Judea.

keyEvents.title: Appeal to the Emperor in the Early Church
keyEvents.description: The tradition of appealing to the emperor, which Paul later made use of, was established during Tiberius' reign. Tiberius' empire set the standard for the relationship between Roman authority and the emerging Christian movement.
